key_findings.finding: The standardized transformation is C(=O)CC → C(O)CC, i.e. reduction of an aldehyde/ketone carbonyl to an alcohol. It is not a carbonyl-to-ether conversion because the product retains only a single C–O bond and does not introduce a second carbon substituent on oxygen.

source_tools.relevance: Reaction query standardization and product mapping

key_findings.finding: Common compatible carbonyl-reduction reagents include NaBH4 (mild, aldehydes/ketones), LiAlH4 (strong, broad reduction), DIBAL-H (especially aldehydes/esters under controlled conditions), BH3·THF or BH3·SMe2, and catalytic hydrogenation such as H2/Pd-C or H2/Raney Ni. For reductive-amination contexts, NaBH3CN or sodium triacetoxyborohydride are compatible, but they generally require an amine and are not the default choice for simple carbonyl-to-alcohol reduction.
